audit.whatIsWrong: late says 'Stacked armor blunts her physical-light kit, and her single-target DOT does almost nothing to a two-item tank frontline', and whys[6] repeats 'stacked armor makes her single-target DOT meaningless'. Riot on Dream-Laden Bough: 'Hitting a champion or monster with a skill will deal additional max Health damage over time.' Riot on Blooming Blows: 'dealing extra true damage on the edge.'
audit.why: This is backwards in the most expensive possible way. Her passive scales with your maximum health, so every HP item makes it hit harder, and the edge of her Q is true damage that ignores resistances outright. The entry tells a tank to build into the two damage types that punish tanks and to expect safety from it.
audit.corrected: Dream-Laden Bough is max-health damage and Blooming Blows' edge is true damage — neither armour nor HP answers her.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (P Dream-Laden Bough, Q Blooming Blows)

audit.whatIsWrong: The condition on Lilting Lullaby appears nowhere. Riot: 'Lillia causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy before falling asleep.' Dream Dust comes from her own hits.
audit.why: Her ult is not a targeted sleep, it is a payout on chip she has already landed. If you have not been touched by a skill since her last hit, a 110s ultimate does nothing to you. That single fact converts 'respect level 6' into an actionable rule — break contact after she lands Q, W or Swirlseed — and it is the best defensive information in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Lilting Lullaby only reaches enemies already carrying Dream Dust; break contact after she lands a skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings claim your knock-up cancels her ult: spikes[3] 'your knock-up cancels her R cast', late 'simply cancel her R mid-cast with your dash', wants.you[2] 'Save R to cancel her R cast'. Lilting Lullaby carries no channel flag and Riot's text describes no cast time to interrupt.
audit.why: The kit file's needsResearch block is empty on purpose, so interrupt eligibility is unknown, not confirmed. Building the entire ult-usage plan on an interaction that cannot be verified from the data is exactly the failure mode the brief warns about, and the replacement fact — the Dream Dust condition — is both verifiable and more useful.
audit.corrected: Interrupt claim removed; the Dream Dust condition replaces it as the counterplay.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (R Lilting Lullaby, no channel flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] describes 'W bounce and E roll'. Watch Out! Eep! is a flat area hit — 'Lillia deals damage in a nearby area, dealing heavy damage in the center'. Only Swirlseed rolls.
audit.why: Half-right names teach the wrong dodge. Eep! has a centre that hurts more, so you sidestep out of the middle rather than watching for a bounce that does not exist. Swirlseed is the one that keeps travelling until it hits a wall or a target.
audit.corrected: Watch Out! Eep! is a centred area hit; Swirlseed rolls.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (W Watch Out! Eep!, E Swirlseed)

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart hands Malphite five of seven stages in a matchup he loses at 46.45% over 887 games, and it contradicts its own whys: whys[2] calls level 3 'a genuine coin flip' and whys[3] says 'call it even' while the chart marks both Malphite.
audit.why: A losing matchup whose chart shows the loser winning five stages is unusable. Aligning the two contested stages with the prose that already calls them even, and conceding the two-item stage where her max-health damage and true damage scale against tank stats, produces a chart that matches both the text and the number.
audit.corrected: win[2] and win[3] to Skill, win[6] to Lillia.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late spike is described as 'Your R is a hard counter to her teamfight' resting on the unverified interrupt, with no acknowledgement of how her damage types scale into your build.
audit.why: The flank knock-up is real and worth keeping; the reason it is not a free win is that the same two items that let you survive to use it are the items her passive scales against.
audit.corrected: Late spike restated with the max-health scaling stated alongside the flank.

edits.before: Save R to cancel her R cast or to flank the carry she sleeps in a fight
edits.after: Break contact after her hits — Lilting Lullaby only touches Dream Dust targets

edits.before: Kite you with W bounce and E roll, never standing still long enough for your Q-W-E to connect
edits.after: Kite with Swirlseed's roll and Watch Out! Eep!, never standing still for your Q-W-E combo

edits.before: Stack her passive DOT on you between trades so you bleed even after you disengage your shield
edits.after: Stack Dream-Laden Bough on you — it is max-health damage, so your HP stacking feeds it

edits.before: Your R is a hard counter to her teamfight — you flank the carry she is trying to sleep-engage and your knock-up cancels her R cast.
edits.after: Your R flanks the carry she sleep-engages, but Dream-Laden Bough deals max-health damage, so the HP you buy to get there feeds it.

edits.before: Your R flanks the carry she sleep-engages or cancels her R mid-cast, and stacked armor makes her single-target DOT meaningless.
edits.after: Dream-Laden Bough deals max-health damage and Blooming Blows' edge is true damage — neither armor nor HP answers her late.

edits.before: At 6 she gets her single scariest tool: R sleeps you and the wake-up hit from her passive plus a W bounce can burst a chunk before your armor stacking ever kicks in — this is her window, respect it and hold your own R to interrupt. Levels 4-5 are a genuine coin flip: your W/E sustain comes online but she still kites your every step, so it lives or dies on whether your Q lands. Once you finish a first armor item your Q slow plus E attack-speed slow finally lets you pin her and out-trade.
edits.after: At 6 she gets her scariest tool: Lilting Lullaby (110s at rank 3) makes you drowsy then asleep and the wake-up hit costs extra — but it only reaches enemies already carrying Dream Dust, so step out after she lands a skill and the ult skips you entirely. Levels 4-5 are a coin flip: your W/E sustain arrives but she kites every step, so it lives or dies on Seismic Shard connecting. A first armor item plus Ground Slam's attack-speed cut finally lets you pin her.

edits.before: This is where you flip the matchup back. Your R is a hard answer to her entire identity — she wants to sleep-engage your carry, and you flank to knock up the carry she is diving or simply cancel her R mid-cast with your dash. Stacked armor blunts her physical-light kit, and her single-target DOT does almost nothing to a two-item tank frontline. The lolalytics 46% is real and earned in lane, but the teamfight is yours: she kites squishies, not an unkillable rock with an unstoppable engage.
edits.after: Your R still answers her identity — she wants to sleep-engage your carry, and you flank to knock up whoever she is diving. Do not read tank stats as safety here: Dream-Laden Bough deals damage as a share of your max health and Blooming Blows' edge is true damage, so armour and HP both fail against her. The 46% is earned. What you can control is her ult — Lilting Lullaby only reaches enemies already carrying Dream Dust, so break contact after she lands a skill.

notes: The entry's late-game thesis was inverted: it told a tank that armour and HP make Lillia harmless, when Dream-Laden Bough deals max-health damage over time and Blooming Blows' edge deals true damage. Both punish exactly the build the page recommends. The 'knock-up cancels her R' claim appeared in three strings and cannot be verified from the kit data — Lilting Lullaby has no channel flag and needsResearch is empty — so it was replaced with the Dream Dust condition, which is stated plainly in Riot's own description and is the stronger piece of advice anyway. Chart corrected on the stages where the prose already said 'even'. Not asserted: whether a knock-up interrupts Lilting Lullaby's cast, and whether Ground Slam's grounding denies her Q's movement-speed stacking.
